title: Netflix Games裁员，团队“转变做游戏的方式”
content:
Netflix Games lays off staff as team “shifts how it approaches making games” – Mobilegamer.biz
Skip to content
Netflix Games has laid off an undisclosed number of staff, according to a flurry of social media posts in the last 24 hours.
[
Update:
a Netflix spokesperson has confirmed to us that a “small number” of games staff were let go but would not confirm a number. They also said Netflix’s broader games strategy remains unchanged and it continues to invest in the games business by hiring staff and launching new games.]
Game director Andrew Brownell said in a
LinkedIn post
that Netflix Games “recently went through a restructuring as the team shifts how it approaches making games”. His role, “along with those of many talented colleagues” was impacted.
According to Brownell, his team had been working on “cloud-streamed action games, phones as controllers, motion and microphone input, gyro and air-mouse controls, and designing around two screens at once”, as well as “concepts for some of Netflix’s biggest franchises, partnering closely with IP owners.”
He named senior concept artist Justin Albers, lead character artist Charles Metze III and senior 3D artist
Courtney Vogel
among those let go, along with “several other incredibly talented folks who’ll share their own news when they’re ready.”
Vertical Slice
reports that other Netflix employees have confirmed the cuts, including one who had been at the company for two and a half years. It’s not clear whether the layoffs are linked to the
roughly 1,000 job cuts
, around 6% of its workforce, that Netflix announced last month.
TV games, played on a smart TV with a phone as the controller, have been a key part of Netflix’s games strategy. But the company didn’t mention games during its third-quarter earnings call in October, Vertical Slice noted.
The cuts follow a string of closures, including
LA studio Night School and Helsinki’s Moonloot
back in August. Netflix has also
closed Squid Game Unleashed maker Boss Fight
, while Spry Fox went independent again in December 2025. That leaves Helsinki’s Next Games as its only first-party studioe.
We have asked Netflix for comment and clarification and will update this story if or when they respond.
